about: A DataTable URL and the view it asks for. tests/table-query.php reads each case with TableQuery::view() and ::filters(), tests/table-view.ts with readView(). Each case's view is laid over the empty URL's view below; its filters over those filters.

cases.what: an empty URL is the defaults
search is trimmed
a plus in search is a space
a percent sign in search is kept
search keeps letters beyond ASCII
search with a null byte is absent, as Postgres refuses it
search that is not UTF-8 is absent, as Postgres refuses it
search that is the replacement character the browser reads invalid UTF-8 as is absent too
a repeated search whose last value has a null byte is absent
sort, direction, page and page size with a null byte or not UTF-8 are absent
sorts by a sortable column
a sort without a direction takes the default direction
a column that is not sortable falls back to the default sort
an unknown direction falls back to the default
sort as an array is not sort
reads the page
page zero is page one
a negative page is page one
a page with a decimal point is page one
a page with a leading zero is page one
a page that is not a number is page one
a page past a billion stops there, past the end of any list
reads a page size on offer
ignores a page size not on offer
ignores a page size spelt another way
a multiple filter reads every value
a multiple filter reads the numbered form PHP rebuilds the page URL in
brackets may come unencoded
a multiple filter drops empty values
a multiple filter without brackets is absent
a select reads its value
a select present but empty overrides its default
a repeated select takes the last value
a select with brackets is absent, so takes its default
a select with a null byte is absent, so takes its default
a select that is not UTF-8 is absent, so takes its default
a repeated select whose last value is not UTF-8 is absent, as PHP never sees the first
a multiple filter drops a value with a null byte or not UTF-8 and keeps the rest
a multiple filter of nothing but values with a null byte is absent
a boolean reads 1
a boolean with a null byte is absent
a daterange reads both ends
a daterange start works alone
a daterange end works alone, and replaces the whole default
a reversed daterange is turned round
a daterange drops a day that does not exist
a daterange drops a date not written as a date input writes it
a daterange end with a null byte is absent, so with both ends like that the range takes its default
a daterange end that is not UTF-8 is absent, and the other end still speaks for the range
a daterange with both ends present but empty overrides its default
a cleared daterange, with neither end in the URL, takes its default
a daterange end with brackets is absent, so takes its default
a named table reads its own parameters

cases.what: a named table ignores another table's parameters
